### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v6.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v6.0.0): 🌈 activate-environment and working-directory

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v5.4.2...v6.0.0)

#### Changes

This version contains some breaking changes which have been gathering up for a while. Lets dive into them:

-   [Activate environment](#activate-environment)
-   [Working Directory](#working-directory)
-   [Default `cache-dependency-glob`](#default-cache-dependency-glob)
-   [Use default cache dir on self hosted runners](#use-default-cache-dir-on-self-hosted-runners)

##### Activate environment

In previous versions using the input `python-version` automatically activated a venv at the repository root.
This led to some unwanted side-effects, was sometimes unexpected and not flexible enough.

The venv activation is now explicitly controlled with the new input `activate-environment` (false by default):

```yaml
- name: Install the latest version of uv and activate the environment
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
  with:
    activate-environment: true
- run: uv pip install pip
```

The venv gets created by the [`uv venv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/environments/) command so the python version is controlled by the `python-version` input or the files `pyproject.toml`, `uv.toml`, `.python-version` in the `working-directory`.

##### Working Directory

The new input `working-directory` controls where we look for `pyproject.toml`, `uv.toml` and `.python-version` files
which are used to determine the version of uv and python to install.

It can also be used to control where the venv gets created.

```yaml
- name: Install uv based on the config files in the working-directory
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
  with:
    working-directory: my/subproject/dir
```

> \[!CAUTION]
>
> The inputs `pyproject-file` and `uv-file` have been removed.

##### Default `cache-dependency-glob`

[@​ssbarnea](https://redirect.github.com/ssbarnea) found out that the default `cache-dependency-glob` was not suitable for a lot of users.

The old default

```yaml
cache-dependency-glob: |
  **/requirements*.txt
  **/uv.lock
```

is changed and should cover over 99.5% of use cases:

```yaml
cache-dependency-glob: |
  **/*(requirements|constraints)*.(txt|in)
  **/pyproject.toml
  **/uv.lock
```

> \[!NOTE]
>
> This shouldn't be a breaking change. The only thing you may notice is that your caches get invalidated once.

##### Use default cache dir on self hosted runners

The directory where uv stores its cache was always set to a directory in `RUNNER_TEMP`. For self-hosted runners this made no sense as this gets cleaned after every run and led to slower runs than necessary.

On self-hosted runners `UV_CACHE_DIR` is no longer set and the [default cache directory](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/cache/#cache-directory) is used instead.

- 0 0 0 points to negative Z in Bevy and positive X in TB. So to go from +X to -Z, we need to do a 90 degree rotation counter clockwise. That's +90 degrees, not -90! 
- Fixed the tests that lookeds like accuracy errors by fixing the underlying math
  - BTW, the original inaccuracy you saw was due there being a sneaky sqrt(2) term in there, as you were pointing from the middle of a unit cube to the corner accidentally
- Fixed angle `-1` and `-2` performing no y-rotation to correct the forward vector
- Found out that mangle is not yaw, pitch, roll but actually [yaw, -pitch, roll](https://github.com/TrenchBroom/TrenchBroom/blob/ef515487adf28bb0008408c185520cdc5f45ce29/common/src/mdl/EntityRotation.cpp#L275-L286)

Note that:
- This is not *entirely* correct either, as the [original TrenchBroom code has nontrivial ways of parsing angles](https://github.com/TrenchBroom/TrenchBroom/blob/ef515487adf28bb0008408c185520cdc5f45ce29/common/test/src/mdl/tst_EntityRotation.cpp#L100-L183)
- This fixes #69 iff https://github.com/TrenchBroom/TrenchBroom/pull/4838 is also merged

#### Changes

This version contains some breaking changes which have been gathering up for a while. Lets dive into them:

-   [Activate environment](#activate-environment)
-   [Working Directory](#working-directory)
-   [Default `cache-dependency-glob`](#default-cache-dependency-glob)
-   [Use default cache dir on self hosted runners](#use-default-cache-dir-on-self-hosted-runners)

##### Activate environment

In previous versions using the input `python-version` automatically activated a venv at the repository root.
This led to some unwanted side-effects, was sometimes unexpected and not flexible enough.

The venv activation is now explicitly controlled with the new input `activate-environment` (false by default):

```yaml
- name: Install the latest version of uv and activate the environment
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
  with:
    activate-environment: true
- run: uv pip install pip
```

The venv gets created by the [`uv venv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/environments/) command so the python version is controlled by the `python-version` input or the files `pyproject.toml`, `uv.toml`, `.python-version` in the `working-directory`.

##### Working Directory

The new input `working-directory` controls where we look for `pyproject.toml`, `uv.toml` and `.python-version` files
which are used to determine the version of uv and python to install.

It can also be used to control where the venv gets created.

```yaml
- name: Install uv based on the config files in the working-directory
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
  with:
    working-directory: my/subproject/dir
```

> \[!CAUTION]
>
> The inputs `pyproject-file` and `uv-file` have been removed.

##### Default `cache-dependency-glob`

[@​ssbarnea](https://redirect.github.com/ssbarnea) found out that the default `cache-dependency-glob` was not suitable for a lot of users.

The old default

```yaml
cache-dependency-glob: |
  **/requirements*.txt
  **/uv.lock
```

is changed and should cover over 99.5% of use cases:

```yaml
cache-dependency-glob: |
  **/*(requirements|constraints)*.(txt|in)
  **/pyproject.toml
  **/uv.lock
```

> \[!NOTE]
>
> This shouldn't be a breaking change. The only thing you may notice is that your caches get invalidated once.

##### Use default cache dir on self hosted runners

The directory where uv stores its cache was always set to a directory in `RUNNER_TEMP`. For self-hosted runners this made no sense as this gets cleaned after every run and led to slower runs than necessary.

On self-hosted runners `UV_CACHE_DIR` is no longer set and the [default cache directory](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/cache/#cache-directory) is used instead.

## 説明
KonomiTVでの録画再生用にtsreplaceを使用する際、Amatsukazeから使用することで、CM解析やCMでのビットレート抑制等を行うことができます。このとき、AmatsukazeではCM解析結果をチャプターファイルに出力します。

この変更は、このチャプターファイルからCM解析結果を読み取りKonomiTVでの録画再生時に反映させるものです。

## 表示例
![KonomiTV_Amatsukaze_chapter_20250424s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7d9ecc6-1a31-44c3-b0d5-e23e2ecb44ee)

## 動機とコンテキスト
CM解析結果をマーカーで示すことで、シーク時の手掛かりとして有用だと思っております。

## 詳細
実装は既存のCMSectionsDetector.pyに追記する形で行いました。

チャプターファイルがあれば、これを開きCM区間を取得します。チャプターファイルがなければ従来通りとします。CM区間については、連続するCM区間は統合しマーカー数を減らすよう実装しました。

あとはDplayer側のhighlightでこれを反映させています。このとき、終了間際のマーカーは省略しています。

## Description

This PR fixes two bugs: 

1.) The charge index calculation was done wrongly for ``groundstates()`` for charge distributions with base = 3. This is now fixed by using ``charge_distribution_to_index_general()``. 
2.) The automatic base detection in the TTS calculation was activated. Hence, the heuristic and exact simulations might be conducted with different bases. This is not desired. The automatic base detection is now turned off, ensuring that the same base is used in both cases.

body:
This pull request introduces multiple changes across several controllers, database models, and supporting files. The most significant updates include adjustments to API endpoints, enhancements to the voting and notification systems, and modifications to database schema constraints. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Controller Updates:
* **`notificacoes_controller.py`**: Updated the `listar_notificacoes` endpoint to use `NotificacaoOutSchema`. Added a new `PUT` endpoint (`/notificacoes/{notificacao_id}/lida`) to mark notifications as read.
* **`recurso_comum_controller.py`**: Renamed the `inserir_recurso_comum` function to `inserir_pedido_novo_recurso_comum` for clarity. Updated the `atualizar_estado_pedido` function to use `estado_data.value` instead of `estado_data.novo_estado_id`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-405e5d2e70d69fbd13876870f8bf326403b4319b8355f08775054052af589b5eL33-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-405e5d2e70d69fbd13876870f8bf326403b4319b8355f08775054052af589b5eL112-L115)
* **`votacao_controller.py`**: Consolidated the `criar_votacao` endpoints for new resources and maintenance requests into a single endpoint, adding support for different voting types. Introduced new endpoints for processing expired votes and handling budget-related voting. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1366ca00de7be8f3b402e421c22d012c947709c0b30d0bfef0a2c7065534ee0cR3-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1366ca00de7be8f3b402e421c22d012c947709c0b30d0bfef0a2c7065534ee0cR55-R72)
* **`websockets_controller.py`**: Migrated WebSocket functionality to use `APIRouter` and introduced dependency-based authentication for WebSocket connections. Added connection registration and unregistration logic.

### Database Schema Adjustments:
* **Primary Key Constraints**: Updated the names of primary key constraints across multiple tables, such as `Categoria`, `Disponibilidade`, `EstadoPedidoManutencao`, and others, to align with new naming conventions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2fccb8144f70b58a148cc0e82ab3093d5005781106a987dee81e0ef39f9131bL15-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c2fccb8144f70b58a148cc0e82ab3093d5005781106a987dee81e0ef39f9131bL27-R27) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c2fccb8144f70b58a148cc0e82ab3093d5005781106a987dee81e0ef39f9131bL79-R79)
* **`Votacao` Table**: Added a new `Processada` column to track whether a vote has been processed. Replaced the `PedidoNovoRecurso` relationship with `Votacao_PedidoNovoRecurso`.
* **Removed Redundant Table**: Deleted the `Sysdiagrams` table and its associated schema.

### Supporting Changes:
* **`.gitignore`**: Added `uploadFiles/` to the ignore list to prevent unnecessary file uploads.

These changes enhance the system's functionality, improve code clarity, and ensure better alignment with project requirements.
